description: Figure 3 is a bar chart that illustrates the automated normalization steps applied to address a higher WER due to spacing errors, date formats, and American spellings in the human transcripts. The chart compares the performance of the Whisper large model with the fine-tuned models (NESAC and SESHA) when compared to the Whisper large model with the same post-processing applied to the human transcript. The x-axis represents the error types, which include Phonetic discrimination and Proper noun errors. The y-axis represents the average word error rate (WER), which is a measure of the difference in the performance of the models. The bars are grouped by error type, with each group containing three bars representing the Whisper large model, the NESAC fine-tuned model, and the SESHA fine-tuned model. The bars are color-coded, with the Whisper large model in black, the NESAC fine-tuned model in blue, and the SESHA fine-tuned model in red. The chart shows that the fine-tuned models have a lower WER compared to the Whisper large model, indicating an improvement in their ability to understand the target accents and proper nouns. The chart also includes a legend that explains the color coding of the bars.
